I replaced the placeholder in `lib/engine/games/palworld.ts` with the full generator. The export name and signature are unchanged, and I edited no other file. `npx tsc --noEmit -p .` exits 0. Partway through, tsc briefly reported errors in `valheim.ts`, which someone else was editing at the time; they were gone by the final run. I read the generated output for all 12 categories and all three models, and it looks like a real UE4SS mod. There is no Lua interpreter on this machine, so none of the generated Lua or busted specs were actually run; I checked them by reading.

The file is about 1,800 lines, roughly four times your 250–450 target. Most of that is Lua template text: each category gets its own module, which is what "sensibly different output per category" took. Say if you want it cut down.

**Layout and file order:** `Scripts/main.lua`, then `Scripts/<snake>/<module>.lua`, then `Scripts/<snake>/effects.lua`, then an empty `enabled.txt`. katara gets only the first three, and they work on their own: config and strings fall back to defaults built into the code. `config` is `Scripts/<snake>/config.lua`, `l10n` is `Scripts/<snake>/lang/en.lua`, and `test` is `spec/<snake>_spec.lua`, a busted spec that stubs the UE4SS globals and tests the module's pure functions.

**Hooks and APIs used:**
- **UE4SS:**
  - `RegisterHook("/Script/Engine.PlayerController:ClientRestart")` with an `IsLocalController()` check, then `ExecuteWithDelay` and `ExecuteInGameThread`.
  - `NotifyOnNewObject`, `FindFirstOf`/`FindAllOf`, `StaticFindObject`, and `LoopAsync` (returns `false` to keep looping).
  - `RegisterKeyBind(Key[...], {ModifierKey.CONTROL})`, `RegisterConsoleCommandHandler`, and `:get()` on hook params.
  - `UEHelpers` for the player controller, world, gameplay statics and Kismet math.
  - `UDataTable:FindRow` / `ForEachRow`, checked against the UE4SS docs.
  - `TArray:ForEach`, and `UEnum:ForEachName`, so enum values are looked up by name at runtime instead of hard-coded.
- **Palworld:**
  - Characters: `PalPlayerCharacter`, `PalCharacter`, `CharacterParameterComponent:GetIndividualParameter()`, and on the parameter `GetLevel`, `GetHP`/`GetMaxHP`/`SetHP` (HP stored ×1000), plus `SaveParameter` fields (`CharacterID`, `IsRarePal`, `Talent_*`, `Rank`, `CraftSpeed`, `OwnerPlayerUId`).
  - Data tables: `DT_ItemDataTable`, `DT_PalMonsterParameter`, `DT_PalDropItem`.
  - World and base: `PalSpawnerStandard`, `PalBaseCampModel`, `PalWorkProgress`, `PalTimeManager`.
  - Items: `PlayerState:GetInventoryData():AddItem_ServerInternal`. I used this path because I couldn't confirm that `PalUtility.GetPlayerInventoryData` exists.
- **Names I couldn't confirm** are tagged `plausible:` in comments and mostly wrapped in `pcall`:
  - the damage hook `PalDamageReactionComponent:ApplyDamageForMP`
  - `IsOtomo`, `GetRidingCharacter`, `GetWork`
  - the time-manager hour accessor
  - `SendSystemAnnounce`, which posts the in-game notices
  - the status-ailment call
  - the base-camp area fields
  - the `DT_PalDropItem` columns
  - the Wwise `PostEventByName`

**What each category generates:**
- **Weapons:** retunes the weapon's damage in its item-table row, keybound charged shot, crit roll, effects applied on hit.
- **Magic:** keybound area spell; damage falls off with distance and it skips your own pals.
- **Items:** keybound satchel that rolls weighted loot into your inventory and raises stack caps.
- **Creatures:** a rare variant rolled as wild pals spawn (lucky flag, stars, IVs, scale, glow); variants' attacks carry the effects.
- **Characters:** your partner pal regenerates, gets teleported back if it strays too far, and spreads effects to nearby enemies.
- **Vehicles:** mount speed raised in its species row, plus a keybound movement boost.
- **Worlds:** stronger spawner groups, extra spawns at night, better drops from the featured pal, dusk/dawn notices.
- **Mechanics:**
  - Prompts about expeditions get a board that sends idle, fed base workers on timed runs. The board is saved to a Lua file next to the mod (sandboxed load) and has a console command.
  - Any other mechanics prompt gets a base-camp loop that speeds up work progress.
  - Your example prompt sometimes routes to Items because "loot" matches that category. Prompts in Items or Mechanics that describe expeditions now get the board either way.
- **Quests:** three stages tracked by polling game state, saved progress, rewards, and a `!quest` chat hook.
- **Interface:** inspects the pal under the crosshair (IVs, passives, work speed) and can be pinned to keep refreshing. UE4SS Lua has no drawing API, so it shows its text through Palworld's notice feed.
- **Audio:** music layers switch between combat, base, night and explore; damage and camp checks drive the switch.
- **Shaders:** sets bloom, vignette, saturation, colour and film grain on the global post-process volume, blending a day and a night look by the in-game hour; keybind toggle and console command.

**Effects:** all 12 effects are mapped in a `Record<EffectKey, …>`. Each has a version that runs inside the damage hook and one that runs anywhere. Only the helper functions and config values an effect actually uses get included.

Sample output from my runs is in `C:\Users\edmem\AppData\Local\Temp\claude\...\scratchpad\pal_out\`. The `out\` folder there was shared with another agent's runs, so I don't rely on it.
